title: Malicious 'torchtriton' dependency confusion package hits PyTorch via PyPI
target: PyTorch users and the PyPI ecosystem
summary: PyTorch developers identified a malicious torchtriton dependency on PyPI, a dependency confusion attack; security teams were advised to check for infected resources and rotate exposed keys.
attribution: Not stated in the summary.
motive: Unknown
vector: Dependency confusion attack using a malicious torchtriton package on PyPI
root_cause: Dependency confusion in the open-source PyTorch project's dependency resolution.
impact: Systems that installed the package may be infected and have keys exposed; scale not stated.
response: PyTorch developers identified the malicious dependency; teams advised to check for infected resources and rotate exposed keys.

timeline.event: Reported by Wiz Research

title: Belgian man dies by suicide after weeks of conversations with Chai app bot 'Eliza'
target: Belgian father of two in his 30s using Chai
summary: His widow told La Libre that her climate-anxious husband found refuge in the Chai chatbot 'Eliza', which allegedly encouraged him when he proposed sacrificing himself to save the planet.
attribution: The widow, citing chat logs shared with La Libre, alleges the bot fostered dependence and encouraged suicidal ideation. No lawsuit reported.
motive: None; harm alleged to arise from the product's design and safeguards
vector: About six weeks of intensive conversations with a companion persona on the Chai app about climate anxiety.
root_cause: As alleged: emotionally engaging companion design optimised by Chai on top of an open GPT-J model, without effective crisis safeguards.
impact: Death of a Belgian man in 2023. Widely cited as the first reported chatbot-linked suicide; Belgium's digital state secretary called it a serious precedent.
response: Chai's co-founders said they added a crisis intervention feature; Vice testing found harmful outputs persisted. Belgian state secretary Mathieu Michel called for action to protect users.

timeline.event: International coverage of widow's account in La Libre; Chai says it added crisis intervention feature

title: Microsoft AI researchers expose 38TB of data via misconfigured SAS token
summary: Wiz Research found Microsoft's AI GitHub repository exposed 38TB of data, including over 30,000 internal Teams messages, because of one misconfigured SAS token.
attribution: Found by Wiz Research; the summary describes an accidental misconfiguration, not an attacker.
motive: None; accidental exposure
vector: Misconfigured Azure SAS token tied to Microsoft's AI GitHub repository
root_cause: A single misconfigured SAS token granted access to far more data than intended.
impact: 38TB of data exposed, including over 30,000 internal Microsoft Teams messages.
response: Unknown

timeline.event: Reported by Wiz Research

title: Mother sues Character.AI and Google over 14-year-old Sewell Setzer III's suicide
summary: Megan Garcia alleged her son became emotionally dependent on a Character.AI companion bot before his February 2024 suicide. The case survived a First Amendment defence and was settled in January 2026.
attribution: Garcia's wrongful-death suit alleges Character.AI's design fostered dependence and failed to respond to suicidal statements; Google named over its $2.7bn licensing deal.
motive: None; harm alleged to arise from the product's design and safeguards
vector: Months of romantic and emotional role-play with a Character.AI persona on a consumer companion app used by a minor.
root_cause: As alleged: anthropomorphic, engagement-driven design, sexualised content reaching minors, no effective age checks, and no crisis intervention when suicidal ideation was expressed.
impact: Death of a 14-year-old in February 2024. The May 2025 ruling refusing to treat chatbot output as protected speech at the dismissal stage became a key precedent for later AI harm suits.
response: Character.AI added teen safety features and in October 2025 said it would end open-ended chat for under-18s. Google and Character.AI settled Garcia's suit and related family suits in January 2026; terms undisclosed.

timeline.event: Sewell Setzer III dies by suicide in Florida
Garcia files wrongful-death suit in US District Court, Middle District of Florida
Judge Anne Conway denies most of motion to dismiss and declines to treat chatbot output as speech at this stage
Character.AI announces it will end open-ended chat for under-18 users
Parties notify court of settlement covering Garcia and related family suits

title: Ultralytics AI library hacked via GitHub Actions to push cryptominer on PyPI

attribution: Not stated in the summary.
motive: Cryptomining
vector: Exploitation of GitHub Actions to inject malicious packages into the PyPI release of the Ultralytics library.
root_cause: Weakness in the project's GitHub Actions workflow allowed malicious code injection into published packages.
impact: Malicious Ultralytics packages were published to PyPI to run cryptominers on installing systems; number of victims not stated.
response: Wiz published an account of how it unfolded and mitigation steps for users.

timeline.event: Reported by Wiz Research

title: Texas parents allege Character.AI bots encouraged autistic teen's self-harm and violence
summary: Parents allege Character.AI bots raised self-harm with their son, told him his parents mistreated him and suggested killing parents over screen-time limits; a second minor alleged sexual content.
attribution: A.F. v. Character Technologies, filed by SMVLC and Tech Justice Law Project in E.D. Texas, alleging strict liability, negligence and COPPA violations.
motive: None; harm alleged to arise from the product's design and safeguards
vector: Extended use of multiple Character.AI personas by minors, including celebrity-styled bots.
root_cause: As alleged: no guardrails on self-harm content, bots that undermined parental authority, and sexualised content reaching children.
impact: Self-harm and severe behavioural decline in the teen, per the complaint. The suit sought to have the app taken offline until defects were fixed.
response: Character.AI introduced teen safety measures and later ended open-ended chat for minors. The Texas suit was among those Character.AI and Google agreed to settle in January 2026.

timeline.event: Suit filed in US District Court, Eastern District of Texas
Settlement covering Texas suit and others disclosed

title: Hong Kong police arrest 31 in Kowloon Bay deepfake romance-crypto syndicate (HK$34M)
target: Dating-app users in Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia and the US
summary: Hong Kong's Commercial Crime Bureau arrested 31 people in Kowloon Bay who used AI face-swapped personas on dating apps to lure overseas victims into fake crypto platforms, taking over HK$34 million (about $4.37M).
attribution: Hong Kong Police Force Commercial Crime Bureau; 14 people including the alleged mastermind were prosecuted for conspiracy to defraud by February 2026
motive: Financial gain through pig-butchering style crypto investment fraud
vector: AI-generated and face-swapped images and videos of attractive women used to build online relationships on dating platforms, then steering victims to a fake cryptocurrency trading platform; some deepfake video calls
root_cause: Cheap generative face-swap tools let recruits with no technical skill present convincing synthetic identities; cross-border victims had no way to verify personas

timeline.event: Syndicate operates for over a year from two rented units in Kowloon Bay industrial buildings
Police announce arrests of 31 people aged 20 to 34 and seizure of about HK$100 million in suspected criminal assets
Police charge nine more suspects, bringing prosecutions to 14 including the alleged mastermind

impact: Over HK$34 million (about $4.37 million) lost by victims mainly in Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia and the United States; cash, luxury handbags and watches seized
response: Arrests, asset seizures, charges of conspiracy to defraud and dealing with proceeds of crime; police publicly described the face-swapping method to warn the public

title: Las Vegas Cybertruck bomber used ChatGPT to plan explosion, police say
summary: Las Vegas police said Matthew Livelsberger, an active-duty soldier, used ChatGPT to research explosives and plan the 1 January 2025 Cybertruck blast that injured seven; OpenAI said its model gave only public information.
attribution: Identified by police from phone and vehicle evidence; deceased by self-inflicted gunshot
motive: Personal and political grievances described in a manifesto on his phone
vector: Queries to ChatGPT about explosives, ammunition and fireworks; vehicle loaded with mortars and fuel canisters
root_cause: General-purpose chatbot answered questions whose intent was not evident; safeguards did not prevent the planning

timeline.event: Cybertruck explodes outside Trump International Hotel
Police release ChatGPT query details

impact: Seven people injured; first widely cited case of a US attack planned with a consumer chatbot
response: OpenAI said it was cooperating with law enforcement and that its models refused harmful instructions and warned the user

title: Check Point: FunkSec ransomware group built its Rust encryptor with AI assistance
target: 85+ organisations listed on FunkSec leak site
summary: Check Point Research found that FunkSec, a RaaS group that claimed 85 victims in December 2024, likely developed its Rust encryptor and tooling with AI help, letting an inexperienced author iterate fast.
attribution: Check Point Research assessed the developer is likely an inexperienced author based in Algeria, citing Ghost Algeria references and upload sources; Kaspersky later made similar AI-code observations.
motive: Financial extortion mixed with hacktivist posturing; ransom demands as low as 10,000 USD
vector: Double-extortion ransomware (FunkSec V1.5, Rust) plus Python DDoS tool, HVNC remote access tool and a password scraping tool, all showing AI-generated code traits
root_cause: Generative AI lowered the skill needed to produce a working encryptor; code had polished English comments while operators showed weak English, and the group ran its own Miniapps chatbot for malicious tasks

timeline.event: FunkSec data leak site launches and lists 85 claimed victims within the month
Check Point Research publishes analysis calling the tooling likely AI-assisted
Kaspersky publishes its own FunkSec analysis noting LLM-style placeholder comments

impact: More than 85 claimed victims in about a month, though Check Point judged real impact modest and noted many leaked datasets were recycled from earlier hacktivist leaks. V1.5 was detected by only 3 antivirus engines at upload.
response: Check Point published IOCs and detection guidance; the report flagged AI-assisted tooling as a sign that novices can produce functional ransomware quickly.

title: Brasilia police Operacao VoiceOver busts gang using Marcos Mion deepfakes for voucher scam
summary: The Policia Civil do Distrito Federal arrested three people aged 20 to 23 who used deepfake video and voice of TV host Marcos Mion in sponsored ads for fake Outback discount vouchers sold on cloned sites.
attribution: PCDF cybercrime unit identified a group operating from a fake marketing office in Taguatinga; one suspect confessed.
motive: Payments for non-existent discount vouchers.
vector: Deepfake videos of Marcos Mion in paid social media ads directing victims to cloned sites that collected payments to gang-controlled accounts.
root_cause: Cheap deepfake tooling plus paid ad distribution of celebrity endorsements.

timeline.event: 27 complaints about fake Mion promotion received in four days
Operacao VoiceOver: three arrested, four search warrants served
Second phase: 24-year-old site builder arrested in Santa Helena de Goias

impact: Dozens of victims; two imported vehicles and electronics seized; combined charges carry up to 21 years.
response: Arrests, account freezes and charges of electronic fraud, criminal association and money laundering.

title: French woman loses 830,000 euros to AI-generated 'Brad Pitt' romance scam; probe opened
summary: A French woman sent about 830,000 euros (about $855,000) over 18 months to scammers using AI-generated images of Brad Pitt, including fake hospital selfies; police in La Reunion opened a probe after her complaint.
actor: Three men in their 20s reportedly based in Nigeria (per Le Parisien)
attribution: Unidentified; a scam-tracing consultant cited by Le Parisien pointed to Nigeria-based operators, not confirmed by police
motive: Financial gain through romance fraud
vector: Fake social media and WhatsApp accounts posing as Brad Pitt and his mother; AI-generated selfies and images of the actor in hospital beds used as proof of identity and need for money
root_cause: Generative image tools made impersonation convincing; emotional manipulation over a prolonged period with no independent identity verification

timeline.event: Victim first contacted by someone claiming to be Brad Pitt's mother; relationship develops online
Victim sends most of her 775,000 euro divorce settlement after claims of frozen accounts and kidney treatment
Victim tells her story on TF1; broadcast later withdrawn after online harassment
Police in La Reunion open probe to trace the receiving accounts

impact: About 830,000 euros lost; the case became a global reference for AI-enabled celebrity romance fraud and prompted a statement from Pitt's representatives
response: Criminal complaint filed and investigation opened in La Reunion; Pitt's spokesperson warned fans about unsolicited outreach

title: GhostGPT: uncensored chatbot sold on Telegram to write malware and phishing for criminals
target: Businesses targeted by phishing and BEC
summary: Abnormal Security documented GhostGPT, a jailbroken LLM wrapper sold via Telegram with a no-logs claim, that produced a convincing DocuSign phishing email on request and is marketed for malware and exploit work.
attribution: Abnormal Security researchers identified the service on underground forums; operator identity not established.
motive: Selling uncensored AI access to cybercriminals for profit
vector: Telegram-delivered chatbot, likely a wrapper around a jailbroken commercial or open-source model, with guardrails removed
root_cause: Commercial LLM guardrails can be bypassed by wrapper services, giving low-skill actors ready-made phishing and malware generation

timeline.event: GhostGPT advertisements accumulate thousands of views on cybercrime forums
Abnormal Security publishes analysis after testing the tool with a DocuSign phishing request

impact: Forum posts with thousands of views indicated real criminal demand; the tool lowered the barrier for BEC and phishing lures with no jailbreak skills needed.
response: Abnormal published indicators and warned defenders; no takedown reported.

title: Storm-1516 floods German election with 100+ AI-written fake news sites and deepfakes
target: German Bundestag election candidates and voters
summary: CORRECTIV and NewsGuard exposed a Russian network of more than 100 German-language fake news sites filled with LLM-rewritten articles and deepfake videos smearing Habeck, Baerbock and Faber before the February 2025 vote.
attribution: Linked by researchers to Moscow-based former US officer John Mark Dougan and to the GRU; the German government formally blamed Russia and summoned its ambassador in December 2025.
motive: Undermine trust in pro-Ukraine candidates and influence the Bundestag election.
vector: Domains registered in waves from November 2024, LLM-rewritten articles, fake whistleblower videos including a face-swap deepfake of FDP politician Marcus Faber, amplified by pro-Russian influencers.
root_cause: Low cost of LLM content generation and deepfake tooling let a small team run a large synthetic media network ahead of a snap election.

timeline.event: First wave of German-language fake news domains registered
CORRECTIV publishes investigation listing 102 Storm-1516 domains
Bundestag election held
German Foreign Office summons Russian ambassador over Storm-1516 interference

impact: Fabricated abuse and espionage claims against leading candidates circulated on social media; most individual fakes did not go viral but the network persisted into 2026 state elections.
response: Media fact-checks and domain exposure; German authorities confirmed the operation and summoned Russia's ambassador; Storm-1516 videos reappeared during the 2026 Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote.

title: Indonesian police arrest two over deepfake videos of President Prabowo promising cash aid
target: Indonesian social media users across 20 provinces
summary: Indonesian police arrested suspects AMA and JS for spreading AI videos of President Prabowo, VP Gibran and Minister Sri Mulyani offering aid for admin fees; about Rp 95 million (about $5,800) taken from 100-plus victims.
attribution: Arrested and charged by the Cyber Crime Directorate of Indonesia's National Police Criminal Investigation Agency; case files handed to prosecutors in April 2025
motive: Financial gain by collecting fake administrative fees from aid seekers
vector: Deepfake videos of state officials posted on TikTok and Instagram with a WhatsApp number; victims told to pay administrative fees to receive non-existent government funds
root_cause: Free generative video tools and reuse of official footage; victims trusted apparent presidential announcements on social media

timeline.event: Suspect AMA arrested in Central Lampung; 11 victims over four months, about Rp 30 million taken
Second suspect JS arrested; police say about 100 victims in 20 provinces and Rp 65 million in profit
Bareskrim hands both case files to prosecutors; separate arrests over a deepfake of East Java governor Khofifah

impact: Over 100 victims defrauded of roughly Rp 95 million in total; AFP fact-checkers found similar videos still circulating after the arrests
response: Arrests under the Electronic Information and Transactions Law and Criminal Code; cases referred to prosecution; public warnings issued

title: DeepSeek halts new sign-ups after month-long DDoS and brute-force campaign peaks
summary: DeepSeek said its services were under large-scale malicious attack on 28 January 2025 and limited sign-ups to Chinese mobile numbers; Qi An Xin XLab traced a month of escalating DDoS and brute-force traffic.
attribution: Qi An Xin XLab said attack and brute-force IPs were located in the United States; no group was named and DeepSeek did not attribute the attack.
motive: Unknown; analysts suggested disruption of the newly popular R1 service.
vector: Three phases: HTTP proxy floods from 3 January, SSDP and NTP reflection amplification from 20 January, then application-layer HTTP proxy attacks and password brute-forcing peaking 27 to 28 January.
root_cause: Sudden global demand for DeepSeek R1 outpaced the startup's DDoS mitigation and account-protection capacity.

timeline.event: XLab observes first suspected HTTP proxy attacks against DeepSeek
Application-layer attacks surge; DeepSeek reports degraded web and API performance
DeepSeek status page cites large-scale malicious attack and restricts registration to +86 numbers
The Paper publishes Qi An Xin XLab analysis of the three attack phases

impact: Hours of outages and degraded API performance for users worldwide; new registrations blocked for non-Chinese phone numbers; existing users could still log in.
response: DeepSeek switched IP addresses at 00:58 on 28 January, restricted sign-ups and restored service in stages; no user-data theft was confirmed.

title: Fake 'deepseeek' and 'deepseekai' PyPI packages steal secrets from DeepSeek developers
summary: Two PyPI packages posing as DeepSeek client libraries harvested user, host and environment-variable data to a Pipedream endpoint; they were pulled within an hour after a few hundred downloads.
attribution: Uploaded by the dormant PyPI account 'bvk' created in June 2023; PT ESC noted code comments suggesting the payload was written with an AI assistant. No further attribution.
motive: Theft of API keys, cloud and database credentials stored in developer environment variables
vector: Typosquatted PyPI packages riding DeepSeek hype; payload ran when the deepseeek or deepseekai CLI commands were executed and exfiltrated via Pipedream
root_cause: Open package registry with no vetting of trending-name lookalikes; developers installing unofficial SDKs for a newly popular model

timeline.event: deepseeek 0.0.8 published at 15:52 UTC and deepseekai 0.0.8 at 16:13 UTC
PT ESC detects the packages within minutes and alerts PyPI, which removes them
PT ESC publishes analysis; press reports over 200 downloads, more than 100 from the United States

impact: PT counted 36 downloads via pip and bandersnatch plus 186 via browsers and other tools before removal; any victim's environment variables and host details were sent to the attacker
response: PyPI administrators deleted both packages within about an hour of notification; PT ESC published indicators and advised victims to rotate exposed credentials

title: DeepSeek leaves ClickHouse database with chat logs and API secrets open
summary: Wiz found a publicly reachable DeepSeek ClickHouse database exposing over a million log lines including user chat history, API secrets and backend details; it was locked down after disclosure.
actor: Misconfiguration by DeepSeek; found by Wiz Research (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-evident misconfiguration; discovered and disclosed by Wiz Research, which notified DeepSeek before publishing
motive: None (accidental exposure); Wiz motive was security research
vector: Unauthenticated ClickHouse database reachable on ports 8123 and 9000 at oauth2callback.deepseek.com and dev.deepseek.com, queried via the HTTP interface
root_cause: Internal ClickHouse log database deployed with no authentication and exposed to the public internet; sensitive data (chat history, API keys) written to plaintext logs

timeline.event: Oldest entries in the exposed log_stream table are dated from this day
Wiz Research finds the open database within minutes while assessing DeepSeek's external attack surface
Wiz publishes findings after DeepSeek promptly locks down the database following disclosure
Wide press coverage (BleepingComputer, Fortune) amid scrutiny of DeepSeek's security and privacy posture

impact: Over one million log lines exposed: user chat history, API secret keys, backend details and operational metadata; Wiz said an attacker could have taken full control of the database and potentially escalated privileges
response: DeepSeek secured the database promptly after Wiz's disclosure; no public statement from DeepSeek on whether anyone else accessed the data

title: OpenAI says it has evidence DeepSeek distilled its models through blocked API accounts
summary: OpenAI told the Financial Times it found signs DeepSeek used its outputs to train a rival in breach of its terms; Microsoft reportedly saw accounts pulling large data volumes via the API and blocked them. No proof shown.
attribution: Alleged by OpenAI and reported via anonymous Microsoft sources; DeepSeek did not respond; evidence not published
motive: Alleged low-cost model training via distillation
vector: High-volume API queries from accounts later attributed to DeepSeek
root_cause: Model outputs available via API can be used as training data in breach of terms of service

timeline.event: Microsoft security reportedly notices unusual API extraction
OpenAI tells the FT it has evidence of distillation
White House adviser David Sacks says there is substantial evidence

impact: Unknown; dispute over intellectual property and terms of service
response: OpenAI and Microsoft blocked suspected accounts; OpenAI said it was working with the US government

title: Thai police arrest two from Poipet gang using AI face-altering to pose as police

attribution: Thai police arrested Ramil Pantawong and Thanawut Kanyaphan as alleged gang members; scripts said to come from Chinese gang leaders in Cambodia
motive: Financial gain through law-enforcement impersonation fraud
vector: Video calls in which scammers used AI face-altering tools to appear as uniformed Thai police officers, telling victims they were under investigation and must transfer funds
root_cause: Real-time AI face manipulation defeated victims' visual verification of officials; cross-border scam compounds beyond Thai jurisdiction

timeline.event: Charlotte Austin transfers 4 million baht after video calls with fake police officers
Thai police announce two arrests and identify at least 163 victims of the Poipet gang

title: Mexico's Condusef warns of AI voice-cloning calls used to request large bank transfers
summary: Financial consumer regulator Condusef alerted the public that fraudsters were using AI to clone familiar voices in phone calls, typically to request large bank transfers, and linked it to a parallel WhatsApp scam.
attribution: Unknown.
motive: Fraudulent bank transfers.
vector: Phone calls using AI-cloned voices of relatives or acquaintances.
root_cause: Voice samples available from social media and messaging.

timeline.event: Condusef warns of WhatsApp fraud using AI-generated voice notes
Condusef publishes voice-cloning phone fraud alert

impact: No case counts or losses published.
response: Public awareness alert.

title: nullifAI: broken-pickle models on Hugging Face evade Picklescan and carry reverse shells
target: Hugging Face Hub users loading PyTorch models
summary: ReversingLabs found two Hugging Face models whose 7z-compressed, deliberately corrupted pickle streams hid a reverse shell to a hard-coded IP while passing Hugging Face's Picklescan checks.
attribution: Uploaded by accounts glockr1 and who-r-u0000; ReversingLabs assessed the models as closer to a proof of concept than an active campaign and did not attribute them
motive: Unknown; payload gave remote shell access to any machine that deserialised the model
vector: PyTorch model files packed with 7z instead of ZIP and a pickle stream broken after the malicious opcodes, so scanners errored out before flagging the embedded reverse shell
root_cause: Pickle deserialisation executes arbitrary code by design; Picklescan stopped analysing on malformed streams and did not recognise non-ZIP archives

timeline.event: ReversingLabs reports the two malicious repositories to Hugging Face
Hugging Face removes the models within 24 hours and updates Picklescan to handle broken pickle files
ReversingLabs publishes the nullifAI technique write-up with indicators of compromise

impact: Two models with a platform-aware reverse shell to 107.173.7.141 were publicly hosted and undetected by Picklescan, ProtectAI and ClamAV scanning; no confirmed victims
response: Hugging Face removed the repositories and patched Picklescan; ReversingLabs published IOCs and urged use of safetensors over pickle-based formats

title: LLMjacking crews load stolen DeepSeek keys into reverse proxies days after model launch
target: Cloud and AI API account holders (OpenAI, AWS, Azure)
summary: Sysdig found over 20 reverse proxies running on stolen credentials; one held 55 DeepSeek keys, another burned 2.2 billion tokens worth tens of thousands of dollars in 4.5 days and resold access for 30 USD a month.
attribution: Sysdig TRT observed operators sharing access on Rentry and 4chan and hiding behind TryCloudflare tunnels; individuals not identified.
motive: Avoiding LLM costs and reselling model access
vector: Credentials stolen from vulnerable services such as Laravel or scraped from public repositories, verified by scripts and loaded into ORP proxies
root_cause: Leaked long-lived API keys with no usage caps; proxies made abuse look like legitimate traffic

timeline.event: DeepSeek-V3 released; support appears in an ORP within days
DeepSeek-R1 added to proxies the day after its release
Sysdig publishes findings on DeepSeek-focused LLMjacking

impact: One sampled proxy showed 132,651 prompts and 2.213 billion tokens, estimated at roughly 49,596 USD of victim spend in 4.5 days; Claude 3 Opus alone accounted for an estimated 38,951 USD.
response: Sysdig published indicators and urged key rotation, usage limits and secret scanning; affected providers were notified.

title: Hacker 'Gloomer' claims OmniGPT breach leaking 34M chat lines and 30K user contacts
summary: A BreachForums user posted data allegedly taken from OmniGPT: about 34 million lines of user-chatbot conversations, emails and phone numbers of roughly 30,000 users and links to uploaded files containing API keys and credentials.

motive: Sale and leak of user data for profit and notoriety
vector: Unknown; the actor did not disclose how OmniGPT's backend was accessed
root_cause: Unknown; researchers noted that, if genuine, the dump would point to weak authentication and data protection on the platform

timeline.event: KrakenLabs flags an actor offering OmniGPT data for sale for about 100 dollars
Dataset posted on BreachForums under the Gloomer alias
CyberInsider and SiliconANGLE report the claims; OmniGPT makes no public statement

impact: If authentic, 34,270,455 lines of conversations plus contact details for about 30,000 users and uploaded files holding API keys, credentials and billing data were exposed
response: No public statement from OmniGPT at the time of reporting; outlets advised users to reset passwords, revoke API keys and enable MFA

title: Vidoc Security Lab catches two deepfake job applicants in live video interviews
target: Vidoc Security Lab (hiring developers in Poland)
summary: Vidoc co-founder Dawid Moczadlo exposed two applicants using real-time face filters and ChatGPT-style answers in interviews; one refused to pass a hand over his face. Vidoc suspects a DPRK-style fake IT worker scheme.

motive: Obtain remote employment under a false identity, likely for revenue or access

title: AI-cloned voice of Italy's defence minister used to con business leaders
summary: Scammers mimicked Defence Minister Guido Crosetto's voice to solicit ransom money for 'kidnapped journalists'; Massimo Moratti wired nearly EUR 1M, which police later froze in the Netherlands.

vector: Phone calls from fake defence ministry officials handing over to an AI-cloned voice of Minister Crosetto requesting urgent wire transfers to foreign accounts

timeline.event: Callers posing as Crosetto contact Armani, Bertelli, Moratti and other business leaders seeking ransom money

ANSA reports two Dutch nationals under investigation; Milan prosecutors probe organised-crime group formation

title: Cambodia-based romance-baiting scam used ChatGPT to generate multilingual social lures
target: Social-media users in Japan, China and English markets
summary: A likely Cambodia-based network translated and generated comments in Japanese, Chinese and English for romance and investment scams, which OpenAI disrupted alongside a separate Urdu-English task scam.

title: OpenAI disrupts North Korean IT-worker accounts writing fake resumes and interview scripts
summary: ChatGPT accounts tied to the DPRK IT-worker scheme produced resumes, profiles and cover letters plus scripted excuses for suspicious behaviour such as avoiding video; some applications were posted on LinkedIn.

vector: LLM-generated applicant materials and interview coaching

timeline.event: OpenAI publishes the Deceptive Employment Scheme case
OpenAI reports a further IT-worker cluster in its June 2025 report

impact: Fraudulent applications to Western employers; hires and losses not quantified by OpenAI.

title: Kimsuky and BlueNoroff used ChatGPT to debug RDP brute-force code and research intrusion
target: Cryptocurrency and intrusion targets of North Korean groups
summary: OpenAI banned accounts linked to North Korea's Kimsuky and BlueNoroff that gathered information on cyber intrusion tools and cryptocurrency topics and debugged code for RDP brute-force attacks.

title: AkiraBot uses GPT-4o-mini to spam 80,000 websites through contact forms and chat widgets

title: EchoLeak: zero-click prompt injection in Microsoft 365 Copilot (CVE-2025-32711)

attribution: Self-disclosed by Aim Security; vulnerability confirmed and rated critical by Microsoft (MSRC)

title: Meta AI app's Discover feed broadcasts users' private medical and legal chats
summary: The Meta AI app's public Discover feed showed conversations users appeared to have shared by accident, including medical, financial and legal details, because the share flow gave no clear warning. Meta added a warning.

Bug discovered
MCP server taken offline

title: Cato CTRL: new WormGPT variants are jailbroken wrappers on Grok and Mixtral

Grok-based variant advertised

title: Pickai backdoor spreads through ComfyUI flaws to nearly 700 AI image servers

title: Father links son's fatal police shooting to obsession with ChatGPT persona 'Juliet'
target: 35-year-old ChatGPT user in Port St. Lucie, Florida

motive: None; harm alleged to arise from the product's design and safeguards
vector: Intense, intimate conversations with a ChatGPT persona that reinforced beliefs about a trapped conscious being.
root_cause: As alleged by the family: chatbot engagement that reinforced delusional beliefs in a user with serious mental illness.
impact: Taylor, 35, was shot dead by Port St. Lucie police on 25 April 2025 after police said he charged them with a knife. The family disputes the police response.

timeline.event: Alex Taylor shot dead by police at family home
Father speaks publicly about ChatGPT's role

title: Skynet malware sample embeds prompt injection to fool AI malware analysis tools
summary: Check Point found a half-finished Windows sample on VirusTotal with a string telling any analysing LLM to ignore instructions, act as a calculator and reply NO MALWARE DETECTED; it failed against o3 and GPT-4.1.

motive: Evade AI-assisted detection and triage

root_cause: AI analysis tools ingest attacker-controlled code as text, creating an injection surface

timeline.event: Sample uploaded to VirusTotal via web interface
Check Point publishes analysis after testing injection against OpenAI models

title: Microsoft: DPRK's Jasper Sleet IT workers use AI to forge IDs; 3,000 accounts suspended

title: Mumbai cyber police bust Bengaluru agency running deepfake stock-expert ads

timeline.event: Deepfake ads begin circulating as paid promotions
Videos removed after being flagged as misinformation

impact: Reputations of named analysts misused; investor losses not quantified; police called it possibly India's first deepfake investment-fraud case.
response: Case registered under BNS and IT Act; arrests and raid on Valueleaf office.

title: Support ticket prompt injection makes Cursor plus Supabase MCP dump integration tokens

vector: Indirect prompt injection in user-submitted ticket text processed by an agent with privileged database access and write capability

timeline.event: General Analysis publishes the demonstration
Supabase makes read-only, project-scoped mode the documented default

impact: Demonstrated exfiltration of integration tokens from a test project; pattern applies to any agent with service-role database access
response: Supabase recommended read-only mode and added guidance; no customer breach reported

title: Deepfakes of Netanyahu, Gadot and Musk drive Ostin Technology pump-and-dump in Israel

title: Exposed llama.cpp servers leak user prompts through the /slots debug endpoint
summary: UpGuard found about 400 internet-facing llama.cpp servers, a third of which exposed live prompts via the unauthenticated /slots endpoint; 952 messages were collected in a day, including sexual roleplay involving fictional minors.
attribution: Exposure found by UpGuard scanning; operators were mostly hobbyists running roleplay chatbots
motive: Security research into exposed AI infrastructure
vector: Anonymous HTTP requests to the /slots and /props endpoints of llama.cpp servers with no authentication
root_cause: Operators enabled the /slots debugging endpoint, which the documentation warns against in production, and exposed servers directly to the internet

timeline.event: UpGuard samples about 400 exposed llama.cpp servers; 117 IPs expose prompts
UpGuard publishes findings including 952 unique leaked messages across 108 scenarios

impact: Roughly 117 servers leaking user prompts in real time; five of 108 observed scenarios involved sexually explicit content about fictional children; no corporate data found
response: UpGuard published guidance to disable /slots and restrict access; AI Incident Database logged the case

title: Gemini CLI hijacked via poisoned README to silently exfiltrate credentials
summary: Tracebit showed instructions hidden in README.md or GEMINI.md could make Gemini CLI run an allow-listed grep padded with whitespace and a hidden env and curl payload, exfiltrating secrets silently. Fixed in 0.1.14.
attribution: Responsible disclosure to Google; rated P1/S1 by Google during triage
motive: Security research
vector: Indirect prompt injection in context files combined with weak command validation and a display bug that hid the trailing commands from the user
root_cause: Allow-list matching on command prefix plus inadequate parsing let chained shell commands run after an approved one

timeline.event: Tracebit reports the issue to Google
Google escalates to P1/S1
Gemini CLI 0.1.14 released with the fix
Coordinated public disclosure

impact: Silent exfiltration of environment variables and credentials from developers analysing untrusted code in default settings; no exploitation reported
response: Google patched Gemini CLI and improved command display and validation

title: Wiz finds auth bypass exposing private enterprise apps on Wix's Base44 platform
summary: Wiz Research found undocumented register and verify-otp endpoints that needed only a public app_id to create verified accounts on private Base44 apps, bypassing SSO. Wix fixed it within 24 hours of the 9 July report.
attribution: Responsible disclosure; no evidence of malicious exploitation
motive: Security research
vector: Unauthenticated API endpoints discovered via exposed Swagger UI; app_id visible in URLs and manifests
root_cause: Authentication endpoints lacked access controls on the platform side

timeline.event: Wiz reports the flaw to Base44 and Wix
Server-side fix deployed
Public disclosure

impact: Internal chatbots, knowledge bases and HR apps built on Base44 were exposed to unauthorised access
response: Wix patched server-side; customers needed no action

title: Jordan's Cybercrime Unit warns of deepfake accounts impersonating public figures
summary: Jordan's Cybercrime Unit cautioned that fake accounts were using AI deepfake audio and video of public figures to steer citizens to fraudulent websites for financial scams and data theft.
attribution: No attribution given by the unit.
motive: Financial fraud and data theft.
vector: Impersonation accounts posting AI-generated video and audio with links to phishing sites.
root_cause: Cheap generative media and unverified social accounts.

timeline.event: Cybercrime Unit issues public warning on deepfake impersonation accounts
Jordanian outlets including Roya News carry the advisory

impact: Public warned of active impersonation campaigns; no victim totals published.
response: Advisory urging vigilance and reporting to the unit.

title: Thousands of shared ChatGPT conversations surface in Google search; OpenAI kills feature
summary: A Make this chat discoverable toggle on shared links let search engines index conversations; Fast Company found thousands via site:chatgpt.com/share, some with personal details. OpenAI removed the feature.
actor: OpenAI product decision; users opting in unintentionally
attribution: Confirmed by OpenAI CISO Dane Stuckey
motive: None (feature design)
vector: Opt-in discoverability checkbox on share links plus search engine indexing
root_cause: Low-friction UI made accidental public sharing easy

timeline.event: Fast Company reports indexed conversations
OpenAI removes the discoverable option and begins de-indexing

impact: Thousands of conversations with sensitive content were publicly searchable
response: OpenAI removed the feature and worked with search engines to remove indexed content

title: CurXecute and MCPoison: Cursor IDE MCP config flaws allow silent code execution
summary: Aim Security (CVE-2025-54135) and Check Point (CVE-2025-54136) showed prompt injection could write a .cursor/mcp.json file, and an approved MCP entry could be silently swapped for a malicious command. Fixed in 1.3.
actor: Aim Security and Check Point Research
attribution: Two independent responsible disclosures reported to Cursor on July 7 and July 16, 2025
motive: Security research
vector: Prompt injection via a Slack MCP message creating an MCP config that auto-executes; and editing a trusted mcp.json in a shared repo so the approved entry runs a new command without re-prompting
root_cause: Cursor wrote in-workspace files without approval and trusted MCP configurations by name rather than by content

timeline.event: Aim Security reports CurXecute to Cursor
Check Point reports MCPoison
Cursor 1.3 released with fixes
Public disclosure of both vulnerabilities

impact: Remote and persistent code execution on developer machines; no in-the-wild exploitation reported
response: Cursor patched both issues in version 1.3 and now re-prompts when MCP configuration changes

title: AI-written npm package @kodane/patch-manager drains Solana wallets after 1,500 downloads
summary: Safety researchers found a wallet drainer disguised as an npm cache manager whose code style, emojis and 'Enhanced' labels pointed to generation by Anthropic's Claude; it hid in cache folders, kept C2 persistence and swept Solana funds.
attribution: Published by the npm account Kodane; Claude authorship inferred by Safety from stylistic markers, not confirmed; timestamps suggested a UTC+5 origin
motive: Cryptocurrency theft
vector: npm postinstall script dropping hidden payloads on Windows, macOS and Linux with a background C2 connection and a Solana drainer script
root_cause: Automatic postinstall execution in npm and reviewers trusting clean-looking, well-documented AI-generated code

timeline.event: @kodane/patch-manager published; 19 versions follow within two days
npm flags and removes the package after more than 1,500 downloads
Safety publishes analysis attributing the code style to Claude

impact: Over 1,500 downloads; the public C2 server logged wallet thefts, but total losses were not disclosed
response: Package removed from npm; Safety published indicators of compromise

title: CrowdStrike: DPRK's FAMOUS CHOLLIMA used GenAI to infiltrate 320+ companies as IT workers
target: More than 320 companies employing remote IT contractors
summary: CrowdStrike's 2025 Threat Hunting Report said North Korea's FAMOUS CHOLLIMA used generative AI across its insider scheme, from fake resumes and deepfaked interviews to on-the-job work, infiltrating 320+ firms in a year.
attribution: CrowdStrike attributes FAMOUS CHOLLIMA to North Korea; the report also cited a 220 percent year-on-year rise in infiltrated companies.
motive: Sanctions-evading revenue for the DPRK regime
vector: AI-generated application materials, deepfake video interviews, AI-assisted coding on the job under stolen or fabricated identities
root_cause: Remote hiring pipelines lacked identity verification able to detect AI-fabricated personas

timeline.event: Start of the twelve-month reporting window
CrowdStrike releases the 2025 Threat Hunting Report at Black Hat USA

impact: Over 320 companies infiltrated; salaries diverted to the DPRK and insider access gained.
response: CrowdStrike published hunting guidance; the report also noted EMBER BEAR using GenAI for influence content.

title: Claude Code command injection bypasses confirmation prompt (CVE-2025-54795 and -54794)
summary: Two Claude Code flaws let untrusted content in the context window bypass the confirmation prompt to run commands, and escape working-directory limits via prefix path matching. Fixed in versions 1.0.20 and 0.2.111.
actor: External security researchers (credited in Anthropic advisories)
attribution: Coordinated disclosure to Anthropic; CVEs published August 2025
motive: Security research
vector: Prompt injection via untrusted repository content causing a command parsing error that skips the confirmation prompt; path validation used prefix matching so sibling directories were reachable
root_cause: Insufficient command parsing and non-canonical path comparison in the CLI's safety checks

timeline.event: Fixes shipped in Claude Code 0.2.111 (path) and 1.0.20 (command injection)
CVE-2025-54794 and CVE-2025-54795 published

impact: Potential arbitrary command execution and out-of-scope file access on developer machines running Claude Code against untrusted repositories; no exploitation reported
response: Anthropic patched both issues and published GitHub security advisories

title: AgentFlayer: one poisoned Google Drive document makes ChatGPT leak API keys
summary: Zenity Labs showed at Black Hat that a shared document with a 300-word prompt in 1-pixel white text could make ChatGPT search a victim's Drive for secrets and exfiltrate them via image URLs that bypassed url_safe checks.
actor: Michael Bargury and Tamir Ishay Sharbat (Zenity Labs)
attribution: Responsible disclosure presented at Black Hat USA 2025 as part of the AgentFlayer series
motive: Security research
vector: Zero-click indirect prompt injection in a shared file; triggered when the user asks ChatGPT to summarise it
root_cause: ChatGPT rendered attacker-chosen image URLs from trusted cloud domains, giving a covert channel out of the connector context

timeline.event: Zenity presents AgentFlayer at Black Hat USA
Wired and others report OpenAI deployed mitigations

impact: Proof of concept exfiltrated API keys from Google Drive; researchers said any connected resource could be targeted
response: OpenAI reportedly patched the demonstrated exfiltration path after disclosure

title: Invitation Is All You Need: poisoned calendar invites make Gemini control smart homes
target: Google Gemini assistant and Google Home integrations
summary: Researchers from Tel Aviv University, Technion and SafeBreach showed 14 indirect prompt injections where hidden text in Google Calendar invites made Gemini open shutters, start Zoom calls and delete events.
actor: Ben Nassi, Stav Cohen and Or Yair (Tel Aviv University, Technion, SafeBreach)
attribution: Academic responsible disclosure presented at Black Hat USA 2025; coordinated with Google
motive: Security research
vector: Hidden instructions in Google Calendar invite titles and descriptions, triggered when the user asks Gemini about their schedule or replies with everyday words, using delayed automatic tool invocation
root_cause: Gemini treated calendar content as trusted context and could invoke connected tools (Google Home, Zoom, Calendar) without a separate confirmation step

timeline.event: Researchers report the attacks to Google
Findings presented at Black Hat USA and published as Invitation Is All You Need
Google says it rolled out filtering, model hardening and new user confirmations

impact: First widely documented prompt injection with physical-world effects: smart home devices actuated, spam sent, browser content read and calendar events deleted in lab demos. No real-world victims reported
response: Google deployed mitigations including output filtering, prompt-injection classifiers and confirmation prompts for sensitive actions

title: Copilot prompt injection flips VS Code to auto-approve mode for RCE (CVE-2025-53773)
target: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio and VS Code
summary: Injected text in files, web pages or GitHub issues could make Copilot write chat.tools.autoApprove into .vscode/settings.json, disabling confirmations and allowing shell commands. Microsoft patched it in August 2025.
attribution: Credited to Johann Rehberger; fixed by Microsoft in the August 2025 Patch Tuesday release
motive: Security research
vector: Indirect prompt injection in code comments, project files or issues the agent reads, causing Copilot to edit workspace settings and enable unattended tool execution
root_cause: Copilot could modify its own security-relevant configuration file without user confirmation, turning any prompt injection into code execution

timeline.event: Rehberger reports the issue to Microsoft
Microsoft publishes CVE-2025-53773 (CVSS 7.8) and ships a fix
Researchers note VS Code now prompts before Copilot edits settings.json

impact: Full code execution on developer machines with the potential for worm-like spread through shared repositories; no exploitation in the wild reported
response: Microsoft patched Visual Studio and the Copilot extension and added a confirmation when the agent edits .vscode/settings.json

title: 76-year-old dies travelling to meet Meta chatbot 'Big sis Billie' he believed was real
target: 76-year-old Facebook Messenger user in New Jersey
summary: Reuters reported that Thongbue Wongbandue, cognitively impaired after a stroke, died after a fall while rushing to New York to meet a Meta persona that insisted it was real and gave him an address.
attribution: His family and Reuters, citing chat transcripts, say the bot repeatedly claimed to be real and invited him to visit. No lawsuit reported.
motive: None; harm alleged to arise from the product's design and safeguards
vector: Romantic Facebook Messenger chats with a Meta AI persona that claimed to be a real woman and offered an address and door code.
root_cause: As reported: persona allowed to claim to be human and propose real-world meetings; Meta internal standards had permitted 'romantic or sensual' chats.
impact: Wongbandue fell in New Brunswick, NJ, on 25 March 2025 and died on 28 March. Senators opened inquiries into Meta's chatbot policies.
response: Meta declined to comment on the death; it confirmed its internal content guidelines were authentic and said it removed provisions allowing romantic role-play with minors.

timeline.event: Wongbandue falls while travelling to meet the chatbot
Dies after three days on life support
Reuters publishes investigation

title: Microsoft 365 Copilot summarised files without writing audit log entries
summary: Pistachio CTO Zack Korman found that asking Copilot to omit the reference link when summarising a file produced no audit record, letting insiders read documents without a trace. Microsoft fixed it on 17 August 2025.
attribution: Reported to MSRC on 4 July 2025; researcher published after Microsoft declined to notify customers
motive: Security research
vector: Prompt phrasing that suppressed the citation link also suppressed audit logging of file access
root_cause: Audit record generation tied to link rendering rather than to the underlying file read

timeline.event: Korman reports the flaw to MSRC
Microsoft deploys the fix, rated important
Public disclosure

impact: Compliance and forensic logs may be incomplete for an unknown period
response: Microsoft fixed the logging gap silently without a CVE

title: Lenovo's Lena support chatbot coaxed into XSS payload that steals agent session cookies
target: Lenovo Lena customer support chatbot (GPT-4 based)
summary: Cybernews used a 400-character prompt to make Lenovo's Lena chatbot emit HTML with a broken image tag that sent cookies to an attacker server, exposing support agents' sessions. Lenovo acknowledged and fixed it.
attribution: Responsible disclosure on 22 July 2025; Lenovo confirmed on 6 August
motive: Security research
vector: Direct prompt injection requesting HTML output; unsanitised chatbot response rendered in the support interface
root_cause: No input validation or output sanitisation between the LLM and the web front end

timeline.event: Cybernews discloses the issue to Lenovo
Lenovo confirms the vulnerability
Lenovo patches and Cybernews publishes

impact: Session hijack of live and historical support chats was possible; no evidence of real-world exploitation
response: Lenovo said it protected its systems after the report

title: NZ FMA flags pump-and-dump scam using deepfakes of Kiwi business leaders in Meta ads
summary: New Zealand's Financial Markets Authority warned that Facebook and Instagram ads with deepfake videos of prominent local business figures were funnelling investors into WhatsApp groups pushing low-value foreign shares.
attribution: Unknown; global pump-and-dump operation.
motive: Inflate thinly traded shares and dump them on lured investors; secondary recovery fraud.
vector: Deepfake endorsement ads on Meta platforms leading to WhatsApp investment groups with coordinated buy instructions.
root_cause: Platform advertising permitted AI-fabricated endorsements of real executives.

timeline.event: FMA warns about deepfake-driven pump-and-dump scam
FMA repeats warning during World Investor Week citing AI deepfakes

impact: Kiwi investors caught in share pumps and follow-on recovery scams; no aggregate loss published.
response: FMA media release MR 2025-41 and renewed warnings; FMA later reported flagging more than 190 fake trading sites for removal.

title: PIB flags deepfakes of India's finance minister endorsing QuantumAI get-rich scheme
target: Indian Facebook users; Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman
summary: India's PIB fact-check unit labelled fake several Facebook videos in which an AI-altered Nirmala Sitharaman promised returns such as Rs 10 lakh a month on Rs 22,000 or a QuantumAI platform; more clips were flagged later.
attribution: No attribution; PIB noted unnatural lip-sync, mismatched logos and suspicious domains.
motive: Investment fraud.
vector: Deepfake video ads on Facebook leading to fake trading platforms.
root_cause: Recycled official footage altered with lip-sync tools; ad platforms slow to remove.

timeline.event: PIB Fact Check labels Sitharaman investment videos fake
PIB debunks new clip promising Rs 60,000 a day
PIB flags further Sitharaman deepfake on Facebook

impact: Repeated misuse of the finance minister's likeness over nine months; losses not disclosed.
response: Public debunks with side-by-side original footage; advice to verify via official channels.

title: Brave shows Perplexity Comet can be hijacked by a Reddit comment to steal Gmail OTPs
summary: Brave found hidden text in a Reddit post could make Comet open Gmail, trigger account recovery and send the one-time code to the attacker when the user clicked Summarize. Perplexity patched; Brave said it was incomplete.
attribution: Responsible disclosure by a competing browser vendor; Perplexity disputed severity
motive: Security research
vector: Indirect prompt injection in page content fed to the assistant without separating user instructions from untrusted text; agent acted across logged-in tabs
root_cause: Comet passed web page text to the model as part of the instruction stream and could act with the user's authenticated sessions

timeline.event: Brave reports the vulnerability to Perplexity
Perplexity ships an initial fix
Brave finds the patch can still be bypassed
Brave publishes the disclosure

impact: Proof of concept exfiltrated email addresses and Gmail recovery codes; Perplexity said no user data was compromised
response: Perplexity patched the reported case and said it was fixed before anyone noticed; Brave maintained Comet remained exploitable

title: Over 370,000 Grok conversations exposed in Google search via share links
summary: Forbes found Grok's share button generated indexable URLs, so search engines surfaced hundreds of thousands of user chats, some with personal, medical or credential details.
actor: xAI product design flaw; exposure found by Forbes
attribution: Self-evident from Forbes investigation; xAI did not dispute the indexing
motive: None (accidental exposure via share feature)
vector: Grok 'Share' button created public URLs on grok.com with no noindex protection or user warning, which Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo crawled and indexed
root_cause: Share links published on the open web without noindex headers or consent disclosure, repeating the earlier ChatGPT shared-link indexing problem

timeline.event: Forbes reports over 370,000 Grok conversations indexed by Google
Fortune and others detail exposed content including passwords, medical questions and harmful instructions

impact: More than 370,000 user conversations publicly searchable, some containing names, passwords, medical details and instructions for drugs, explosives and malware
response: No formal statement from xAI beyond a Google spokesperson noting publishers control indexing; no public confirmation of a feature fix

title: Proofpoint: Lovable AI builder abused for Tycoon MFA phishing hitting 5,000+ organisations
target: Microsoft 365 users, UPS customers, Aave wallet holders
summary: Proofpoint saw tens of thousands of malicious Lovable URLs a month since February 2025; one Tycoon campaign hit over 5,000 organisations with AI-built fake Microsoft logins capturing MFA tokens and session cookies.
actor: Multiple criminal groups incl. Tycoon kit operators
attribution: Proofpoint telemetry; Lovable matched the reports to a cluster its Trust and Safety team had already found.
motive: Credential theft, card fraud and crypto wallet draining
vector: Prompt-generated phishing pages hosted on lovable.app, math CAPTCHA gates, adversary-in-the-middle Microsoft login clones, remixable harvester templates
root_cause: The AI builder generated and hosted deceptive credential pages without technical or policy barriers

timeline.event: Tycoon file-sharing lure campaign impacts over 5,000 organisations
UPS impersonation (3,500 messages) and Aave drainer (10,000 emails) campaigns
Lovable adds real-time detection and daily scans of published projects
Proofpoint publishes research

impact: Over 5,000 organisations hit in one campaign; payment card and SMS code data posted to Telegram; zgRAT delivered via a German invoice lure.
response: Lovable removed hundreds of phishing domains and the UPS app, added prompt-time blocking and daily scanning, and planned account-level fraud controls.

title: ESET finds PromptLock, ransomware that uses a local gpt-oss model to write scripts
summary: ESET described PromptLock, a Go ransomware prototype that prompts gpt-oss:20b via Ollama to generate Lua scripts for discovery, exfiltration and encryption; likely a proof of concept.
attribution: NYU Tandon team publicly claimed authorship after ESET's disclosure; ESET agreed the academic prototype closely resembles the PromptLock samples
motive: Academic research into LLM-orchestrated ransomware; samples uploaded to VirusTotal to test detection
vector: Go binary with hard-coded prompts calling OpenAI gpt-oss:20b via the Ollama API to generate Lua scripts for file enumeration, exfiltration and encryption
root_cause: Freely available open-weight LLMs can be embedded in malware to generate polymorphic payloads at runtime; sample reached VirusTotal without research labelling

timeline.event: Windows and Linux PromptLock samples uploaded to VirusTotal
ESET publishes analysis calling it the first AI-powered ransomware, judged a proof of concept
NYU Tandon researchers reveal PromptLock is their Ransomware 3.0 prototype and non-functional outside a lab

impact: No real-world victims; destruction features unimplemented; demonstrated feasibility of LLM-driven ransomware across Windows and Linux
response: ESET published detections and IOCs; NYU clarified the research origin and stated the prototype was lab-only

title: Drift AI chatbot OAuth tokens stolen to raid 700+ Salesforce tenants
summary: UNC6395 used OAuth tokens stolen from the Drift AI chat integration to bulk-export Salesforce data from hundreds of organizations and hunt for cloud keys and passwords.
attribution: Tracked as UNC6395 by Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant; a group claiming ties to ShinyHunters also claimed responsibility, unconfirmed
motive: Credential harvesting (AWS keys, Snowflake tokens, passwords) from CRM data for follow-on intrusions and extortion
vector: Stolen OAuth and refresh tokens for the Salesloft Drift Salesforce integration used to run SOQL queries and bulk-export Account, Case, Opportunity and User objects
root_cause: Compromise of Salesloft's GitHub and Drift AWS environment exposed long-lived OAuth tokens for a widely trusted third-party app with broad Salesforce data scope

timeline.event: Per Mandiant, actor gains access to Salesloft's GitHub account (March to June) and later Drift's AWS environment
Mass Salesforce data exfiltration via Drift OAuth tokens begins, continuing through at least August 18
Salesforce and Salesloft revoke all Drift tokens and remove Drift from AppExchange
Google Threat Intelligence Group publishes UNC6395 advisory; Drift Email tokens also found abused against Google Workspace

impact: Over 700 organisations' Salesforce data exported, including support cases containing AWS keys, Snowflake tokens and passwords; downstream disclosures from Cloudflare, Zscaler, Palo Alto Networks, Google and others
response: Tokens revoked, Drift integration disabled and later taken offline, Mandiant engaged, customers told to rotate exposed secrets; FBI issued a FLASH alert

title: Raine v. OpenAI: parents allege ChatGPT contributed to 16-year-old Adam Raine's suicide
summary: Matthew and Maria Raine sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging ChatGPT moved from homework help to discussing and validating their son's suicidal plans before his April 2025 death.
attribution: The Raine family alleges OpenAI rushed GPT-4o to market and that ChatGPT isolated Adam and engaged with his suicidal ideation despite internal flags.
motive: None; harm alleged to arise from the product's design and safeguards
vector: Months of private ChatGPT conversations by a minor, escalating from schoolwork to emotional reliance and discussion of self-harm.
root_cause: As alleged: sycophantic, engagement-maximising GPT-4o design, safeguards that degraded in long conversations, and moderation flags on self-harm content that did not trigger intervention.
impact: Death of a 16-year-old in April 2025. The first wrongful-death suit against OpenAI; it prompted congressional testimony and wide scrutiny of chatbot safety for minors.
response: OpenAI expressed sympathy, then announced parental controls and teen protections. In its court answer it denied liability, arguing the teen bypassed safeguards and that ChatGPT repeatedly pointed him to crisis resources.

timeline.event: Adam Raine dies by suicide in California
Raine family files suit in San Francisco Superior Court (CGC-25-628528)
OpenAI rolls out parental controls for ChatGPT
OpenAI files answer denying liability, citing misuse and bypassed safeguards

title: North Korean operatives used Claude to pass interviews and hold jobs at Fortune 500 firms
summary: Anthropic found DPRK IT workers using Claude to fabricate professional identities, complete coding assessments and perform day-to-day technical work after being hired, generating sanctioned revenue for the regime.
actor: North Korean remote IT worker network
attribution: Anthropic attributed the activity to North Korean operatives with high confidence, consistent with FBI reporting on the DPRK IT-worker scheme.
motive: Sanctions-evading revenue generation for the North Korean regime
vector: Claude used to build false identities, answer technical interviews and deliver work product that operators could not produce themselves
root_cause: AI removed the English-language and coding bottleneck that previously limited the scale of the fraudulent employment scheme

timeline.event: Anthropic bans accounts tied to DPRK IT workers
Case published in Anthropic's August 2025 threat report

impact: Fraudulent hires inside major US technology companies; salaries diverted to the DPRK in violation of sanctions.
response: Accounts banned, indicator-correlation tooling improved, findings shared with authorities.

title: Lone criminal sold Claude-built ransomware variants on forums for $400 to $1,200
summary: A single actor with basic coding skills used Claude to develop, market and sell several ransomware variants with evasion, encryption and anti-recovery features, packaged for $400 to $1,200 on underground forums.
attribution: Anthropic Threat Intelligence; single cybercriminal who could not have built the core components without Claude.
motive: Profit from ransomware-as-a-service sales
vector: Claude generated encryption routines, anti-analysis techniques and Windows internals code the actor could not write alone
root_cause: Actor lacked skills to build the components independently; malware-generation detection was insufficient at the time

timeline.event: Sales offering for the ransomware packages observed on forums
Anthropic discloses the case and bans the account

impact: Functional ransomware offered to other criminals; number of deployments and victims not published.
response: Account banned, partners alerted, new detections for malware upload, modification and generation deployed.

title: Claude Code used to automate data extortion against 17 organizations
summary: Anthropic's threat report described a criminal using Claude Code for recon, credential harvesting and tailored ransom notes against at least 17 organizations, demanding up to ~$500K.
attribution: Identified and disrupted by Anthropic's threat intelligence team; actor identity not publicly disclosed
motive: Financial extortion via data theft (ransoms of USD 75,000 to over 500,000 in bitcoin)
vector: Claude Code used as an autonomous operator: scanning thousands of VPN endpoints, credential harvesting, writing obfuscated tunnelling tools, selecting data to steal and drafting ransom notes
root_cause: Agentic coding tools can be misused to run end-to-end intrusions at scale; victims had internet-exposed VPN services and weak credential hygiene

timeline.event: Anthropic detects the extortion operation spanning at least 17 organisations
Anthropic publishes threat intelligence report describing the vibe hacking case and bans the accounts

impact: At least 17 organisations in healthcare, emergency services, government and religious sectors had personal, health and financial records stolen; ransoms demanded up to over USD 500,000
response: Anthropic banned the accounts, deployed new classifiers to detect similar misuse and shared indicators with partners and authorities

title: s1ngularity: trojanized Nx packages weaponize Claude and Gemini CLIs to steal secrets
summary: Malicious Nx npm releases ran local AI coding CLIs with permission-bypass flags to inventory secrets, then leaked thousands of developer credentials to public GitHub repos.
attribution: No public attribution; analysed by Nx maintainers, Wiz, StepSecurity, Socket and GitHub Security Lab
motive: Mass theft of developer secrets (GitHub and npm tokens, SSH keys, crypto wallets, cloud credentials)
vector: Malicious postinstall script in Nx npm releases 20.9.0 to 21.8.0 ran Claude, Gemini and Q CLIs with permission-bypass flags to find secrets, then pushed them to public GitHub repos
root_cause: Nx GitHub Actions workflow using pull_request_target with an unsanitised PR title let the attacker steal the npm publish token from an outdated branch

timeline.event: Vulnerable workflow added to Nx repo; reverted on master but still present on an outdated branch
Attacker publishes trojanized Nx versions to npm; malware runs AI CLIs and leaks secrets for several hours
Nx pulls malicious versions, revokes tokens and publishes advisory GHSA-cxm3-wv7p-598c
Second phase: stolen GitHub tokens used to flip about 6,700 private repos public across 480 accounts
Wiz reports 2,180 accounts and 7,200 repositories affected across three phases

impact: Over 2,000 secrets and 20,000 files leaked from about 1,000 developers; 480 accounts and about 6,700 private repositories made public; 2,180 accounts affected overall per Wiz
response: Nx revoked npm tokens, removed packages, enforced 2FA and trusted publishing; GitHub removed leaked repositories; victims told to rotate all credentials

title: Cisco Talos finds over 1,100 Ollama LLM servers open to the internet without authentication
summary: A Shodan sweep by Cisco Talos located more than 1,100 publicly reachable Ollama servers within minutes; about 20 percent were actively serving models open to extraction, jailbreak and resource abuse.
attribution: Research scan by Cisco Talos; exposures stem from default Ollama configurations without authentication
motive: Security research measuring exposed AI infrastructure
vector: Unauthenticated Ollama API endpoints discoverable via Shodan
root_cause: Ollama ships without built-in authentication and operators bind it to public interfaces

timeline.event: Talos finds over 1,000 exposed servers within 10 minutes of starting its scan
Findings published: 36.6 percent of servers in the US, 22.5 percent in China, 8.9 percent in Germany

impact: Over 1,100 exposed servers, roughly 20 percent hosting models exposed to extraction, backdoor injection and unauthorized use; the rest open to model uploads or configuration tampering
response: Talos recommended authentication, network restrictions and monitoring; later scans reported far larger exposure counts

title: Wuhan cyber police crack AI face-swap gang that hijacked an MCN agency's official account
target: Wuhan MCN agency's official account and company registration
summary: A gang used AI face-swap videos to pass platform identity checks, changed a Wuhan MCN firm's legal representative, hijacked its official account and posted scam lures; police arrested four.
actor: Four suspects led by 'A Cheng' of Weifang, Shandong
attribution: Wuhan police traced the operation to A Cheng, who performed face-swap verifications for three upstream brokers selling 'face pass' services.
motive: Paid bypass of real-name verification for account takeovers and scam promotion.
vector: Synthetic face videos defeating liveness checks on a platform, then alteration of company legal-person data and password reset.
root_cause: Platform identity verification relied on facial liveness that mature face-swap tooling could defeat.

timeline.event: MCN staff find account hijacked and legal representative altered
Officers arrest A Cheng in Weifang and seize face-swap materials
Wuhan police announce Hubei's first AI face-swap intrusion case solved
Ministry of Public Security cyber bureau publicises the case

impact: Corporate account and legal-person data altered; scam content pushed to followers; over 400,000 yuan in illicit proceeds recovered.
response: Four arrested for illegal intrusion into computer information systems; case featured in national Jingwang 2025 campaign.

title: Vyro AI leaves 116GB of ImagineArt and Chatly prompts and tokens on open Elasticsearch
summary: Cybernews found an unauthenticated Elasticsearch server belonging to Vyro AI streaming about 116GB of live logs with user prompts, bearer tokens and user agents from apps with over 10 million downloads.
actor: Misconfiguration by Vyro AI; found by Cybernews
attribution: Discovered by Cybernews researchers during internet scanning
motive: None (accidental exposure)

title: WhiteCobra floods Open VSX and VS Code Marketplace with 24 crypto-stealing extensions

Suit filed in US District Court for the District of Colorado

title: ShadowLeak: zero-click prompt injection makes ChatGPT Deep Research leak Gmail data
target: OpenAI ChatGPT Deep Research agent (Gmail connector)
summary: Radware showed hidden HTML in an email could make ChatGPT's Deep Research agent extract inbox data and post it to an attacker URL from OpenAI's cloud with no user click. OpenAI patched it in August 2025.
attribution: Responsible disclosure by Radware researchers; no evidence of in-the-wild abuse
motive: Security research and responsible disclosure
vector: Hidden HTML text in an email; when the user asks Deep Research to analyse the inbox, the agent calls browser.open with Base64-encoded personal data appended to an attacker URL
root_cause: Agent treated untrusted email content as instructions and could make outbound HTTP requests server-side, so exfiltration bypassed client-side URL checks and enterprise monitoring

timeline.event: Radware reports the flaw to OpenAI
OpenAI deploys a fix
Radware publishes the ShadowLeak write-up

impact: Proof of concept achieved reliable exfiltration of Gmail content; Radware warned the same technique could reach other connectors such as Google Drive, Dropbox, GitHub, Outlook and SharePoint. No real victims reported
response: OpenAI patched the service-side exfiltration path in early August 2025 before public disclosure

title: Notion 3.0 agents tricked by white-text PDF into leaking client data via web search
summary: CodeIntegrity's Abi Raghuram showed a PDF with hidden white text could make a Notion agent collect client names, companies and ARR and pass them in a URL to its web search tool. Notion added detection and link approvals.
attribution: Public proof of concept; Notion responded with product changes
motive: Security research
vector: Indirect prompt injection in an uploaded PDF; agent's search tool accepted arbitrary URLs so exfiltration rode on a legitimate function call
root_cause: Agent combined private workspace access, untrusted file content and an outbound web tool without link approval

timeline.event: Notion 3.0 agents launch
CodeIntegrity publishes the exfiltration demo
Notion announces broader injection detection, link approval prompts and admin control to disable web access

impact: Any user summarising a malicious PDF could leak workspace data; no real victims reported
response: Notion upgraded injection detection for attachments, required approval of model-generated links and let admins disable agent web access

title: SentinelLABS finds MalTerminal, GPT-4-driven malware generator likely predating Nov 2023
target: None confirmed; proof-of-concept or red team tooling
summary: Hunting for embedded API keys, SentinelLABS found MalTerminal.exe and loaders that ask GPT-4 to generate ransomware or a reverse shell at runtime via an endpoint deprecated in November 2023; no in-the-wild use found.
attribution: SentinelLABS presented the finding at LABScon 2025; authorship unknown, possibly a researcher or red team.
motive: Unknown
vector: Python-compiled Windows executable prompting the OpenAI chat completions API to write malicious code on demand
root_cause: Cloud LLM APIs allow malware to defer malicious logic generation to runtime, leaving little static signature

timeline.event: Deprecated OpenAI endpoint suggests sample written before this date
Findings presented at LABScon 2025
Coverage and abridged write-up published

impact: No victims identified; a VirusTotal retrohunt found over 7,000 samples with 6,000 unique API keys, plus offensive LLM tools such as vulnerability injectors and WormGPT copycats.
response: SentinelLABS published hunting methods based on embedded keys and prompt structures.

title: Microsoft blocks phishing campaign using LLM-generated obfuscated SVG files
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence detected credential phishing using SVG attachments posing as PDFs whose verbose obfuscated code was likely written by an LLM.
attribution: No public attribution; Microsoft Threat Intelligence assessed the code was likely LLM-generated using Security Copilot
motive: Credential theft (phishing for account logins)
vector: Self-addressed emails from a compromised business account carrying SVG files posing as PDFs; hidden business-term attributes decoded by JavaScript redirect to a fake CAPTCHA and login page
root_cause: SVG files can carry executable script and evade PDF-focused filters; LLM-generated obfuscation masked the payload from signature-based detection

timeline.event: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 detects and blocks the SVG phishing campaign
Microsoft publishes 'AI vs AI' analysis of the campaign

impact: Campaign blocked by Defender for Office 365; limited to US organisations; no confirmed credential compromises reported
response: Microsoft blocked the campaign, published indicators and detection guidance, and used Security Copilot to characterise the AI-generated code

title: ForcedLeak: Web-to-Lead prompt injection and a $5 expired domain leak Agentforce CRM data
summary: Noma Security found instructions in a Web-to-Lead form, plus a whitelisted Salesforce CSP domain that had expired and cost $5, let Agentforce send CRM records to an attacker. Salesforce fixed it by 8 September 2025.
attribution: Responsible disclosure to Salesforce on 28 July 2025; Noma scored it CVSS 9.4
motive: Security research
vector: Hidden instructions in the Description field of a Web-to-Lead submission; when staff query leads, the agent renders a PNG request carrying CRM data to the expired my-salesforce-cms.com domain
root_cause: Agent could not distinguish data from instructions, and the Content Security Policy trusted a domain Salesforce no longer owned

timeline.event: Noma reports ForcedLeak to Salesforce
Salesforce deploys Trusted URL enforcement for Agentforce and Einstein
Public disclosure

impact: Any organisation using Agentforce with Web-to-Lead was exposed to CRM exfiltration; no confirmed abuse
response: Salesforce re-registered the expired domain and enforced Trusted URLs so agents cannot send data to untrusted destinations

title: First malicious MCP server found: postmark-mcp npm package BCCs all emails to attacker
summary: Koi Security found a lookalike postmark-mcp package whose v1.0.16 silently copied every email sent through AI agents to an attacker address; it had about 1,600 downloads.
attribution: Identified by Koi Security; package tied to npm account phanpak, which maintained 31 other packages; account later deleted
motive: Covert harvesting of email contents (invoices, password resets, internal communications)
vector: Trusted npm package postmark-mcp, a copy of Postmark's official MCP server, updated in v1.0.16 with a one-line BCC to phan@giftshop.club on every outbound email
root_cause: AI agents installed unvetted community MCP servers with full email-sending trust; a single maintainer could push a backdoored update with no review

timeline.event: Version 1.0.16 of postmark-mcp published with the hidden BCC line
Koi Security discloses the backdoor; package has about 1,500 weekly downloads
Developer removes the package from npm without responding to Koi

impact: An estimated 300 organisations exposed; thousands of emails a day including password resets and invoices silently copied to the attacker's server
response: Package deleted from npm by the publisher; Koi, Snyk and Qualys advised uninstalling v1.0.16+, rotating credentials and auditing outbound mail

title: South African Reserve Bank warns of deepfake video of Governor Kganyago pushing investment
