motive: Lure investors to a fraudulent platform using central bank credibility.
vector: AI-generated video with cloned voice of the governor shared on social media directing viewers to a suspicious platform.
root_cause: Public figures' speeches provide ample training material for voice and face cloning.

timeline.event: SARB flags deepfake video on X
South African media report the warning

impact: No losses disclosed; coverage cited reports of a 1,200 percent rise in deepfake fraud cases in South Africa.
response: Public warning; SARB urged verification before trusting online content.

title: Gemini Trifecta: log, search-history and browsing flaws let Gemini exfiltrate user data
target: Google Gemini (Cloud Assist, Search, Browsing Tool)
summary: Tenable disclosed three Gemini flaws: prompts in User-Agent headers ran when Cloud Assist summarised logs, injected browser-history queries became trusted context, and the browsing tool leaked data. Google fixed all.
attribution: Responsible disclosure to Google; remediated before publication
motive: Security research
vector: Poisoned HTTP log entries, JavaScript that injects queries into a victim's Chrome history, and prompts that make the browsing tool embed saved locations in outbound requests
root_cause: Gemini integrations treated logs, search history and web content as trusted context without separation from user intent

timeline.event: Tenable reports the three issues to Google
Tenable publishes the Gemini Trifecta research after Google remediation

impact: Potential exposure of saved information and location data and compromise of cloud resources for Gemini users; no exploitation reported
response: Google stopped rendering hyperlinks in log summaries, hardened the search personalisation model and remediated the browsing tool

title: CamoLeak: hidden PR comments make GitHub Copilot Chat leak private repo secrets

title: Path traversal in Smithery MCP hosting exposed root access to 3,000 hosted MCP servers

motive: Security research into MCP hosting platforms
vector: Setting dockerBuildPath to a parent directory so the Docker build context included the builder's .docker/config.json containing an overprivileged fly.io token
root_cause: Unvalidated build configuration plus a shared, overprivileged platform credential with access to the fly.io Machines API

timeline.event: GitGuardian discovers the path traversal
Proof of concept disclosed to Smithery, which acknowledges it the same day
Partial fix deployed and compromised token rotated
Complete fix deployed
GitGuardian publishes the write-up

impact: Demonstrated root command execution on hosted MCP servers and capture of a customer API key in traffic; secrets of thousands of customers across hundreds of services could have been exposed
response: Smithery rotated the token and fixed the build path validation within two days of disclosure

title: Hacker uses Claude to breach Mexican agencies and steal 150GB of tax and voter data

motive: Theft and likely resale of tax, voter and personal data

title: OnlyFake creator pleads guilty to selling 10,000+ AI-made fake IDs for KYC fraud

attribution: FBI undercover purchases in 2024; arrested in Romania and extradited to the US in September 2025; guilty plea in SDNY

timeline.event: Media coverage of OnlyFake; operator deletes emails and routes crypto through multiple wallets
FBI undercover agents make controlled purchases through June 2024
Nazarenko extradited from Romania
Guilty plea announced; sentencing set for June 2026 with a 15-year maximum

title: Iran-nexus Dust Specter hits Iraqi officials with malware showing generative AI traces

timeline.event: Earlier Dust Specter page disguised as Webex invite reuses TWINTALK C2 domain
Campaign against Iraqi officials detected by ThreatLabz
Zscaler publishes analysis

impact: Government officials targeted with remote access and exfiltration tooling; victim count not disclosed.

HP publishes Threat Insights Report

title: Father alleges Google Gemini drew son into delusional 'mission' before his suicide

timeline.event: Jonathan Gavalas dies by suicide (early October 2025)
Wrongful-death suit filed in US federal court in San Jose

Microsoft publishes AI as tradecraft report naming Coral Sleet

Microsoft details AI tradecraft and reports thousands of accounts disrupted

title: Autonomous AI agent breaches McKinsey's Lilli chatbot platform in two hours
summary: CodeWall's offensive agent found SQL injection via unauthenticated Lilli API endpoints, claiming read-write access to 46.5M chat messages and system prompts; McKinsey patched within a day.
actor: CodeWall autonomous offensive AI agent (responsible disclosure)
attribution: Self-disclosed by CodeWall; McKinsey confirmed patching
motive: Security research demonstrating autonomous agent capability
vector: 22 unauthenticated API endpoints; SQL injection via JSON keys concatenated into queries, plus broken access control on user IDs
root_cause: Unauthenticated endpoints and unsanitized JSON field names in SQL, with prompts, files, configs and user data stored in one backend

timeline.event: CodeWall agent gains read-write access in under two hours in late February
CodeWall notifies McKinsey security team
McKinsey patches exposed endpoints and takes dev environment offline
CodeWall publishes findings

impact: Claimed access to 46.5 million chat messages, 728,000 files, 57,000 user accounts and 95 writable system prompts; no malicious exploitation reported.
response: McKinsey patched within a day and took the environment offline; CodeWall and Promptfoo published analyses.

title: CISA confirms active exploitation of max-severity n8n expression injection RCE
target: Self-hosted n8n AI workflow automation servers
summary: CISA added CVE-2025-68613, a CVSS 9.9 expression-injection flaw in n8n's workflow engine, to its KEV catalog; over 24,700 unpatched instances were exposed, each typically holding cloud keys, OAuth tokens and database passwords.
attribution: CISA confirmed in-the-wild exploitation without naming actors; no public details of the attacks
motive: Unknown; access to n8n yields stored credentials for connected SaaS, cloud and AI services
vector: Authenticated low-privilege user injects payloads into workflow expressions that execute without isolation, gaining code execution as the n8n process
root_cause: Insufficiently sandboxed expression evaluation in n8n versions 0.211.0 through 1.122.0

timeline.event: n8n publishes advisory GHSA-v98v-ff95-f3cp and fixes in 1.120.4, 1.121.1 and 1.122.0
Shadowserver counts more than 24,700 unpatched instances online
CISA adds CVE-2025-68613 to KEV with a March 25 federal deadline

impact: Full takeover of vulnerable instances with access to secrets and the ability to modify workflows; Resecurity estimated over 103,000 of 230,000 active users were vulnerable
response: Vendor patch available since December 2025; CISA ordered federal agencies to remediate by March 25, 2026

title: AI-generated ClickFix sites on typosquatted domains deliver SmartRAT
summary: In March 2026 Zscaler ThreatLabz saw typosquatting domains hosting malicious content made with AI website builders to run ClickFix lures delivering SmartRAT.

motive: Malware delivery (SmartRAT).
vector: Typosquatted domains with convincing lures generated by AI-powered website creation tools, using ClickFix social engineering.
root_cause: AI website builders let attackers produce convincing lures quickly and at scale.
impact: Unknown; victim numbers are not stated.
response: Zscaler ThreatLabz observed and published an analysis of the campaign.

timeline.event: Reported by Zscaler ThreatLabz

title: Cybernews: 45 of 98 unauthenticated Open WebUI servers already running miners and stealers
summary: Cybernews researchers found 98 Open WebUI servers with authentication disabled and over 2,000 allowing open sign-up; 45 of the unauthenticated hosts carried a cryptominer and infostealer operation seen in 14 variants with Discord webhook alerts.
attribution: Single malware source tracked through 14 versions; operator not identified

vector: Open WebUI instances with authentication off or open registration; payloads hidden by repeated byte reversal, base64 and zlib layers
root_cause: Operators disabling authentication or leaving sign-up open on internet-facing AI chat front ends; two undocumented API routes lacking access control

timeline.event: Cybernews publishes the scan: 98 unauthenticated instances, 45 compromised, 2,000 plus with open registration
Two information disclosure flaws reported to Open WebUI Inc.; report closed without response

impact: Nearly half of unauthenticated servers compromised for mining and data theft; attackers gained access to chats, uploaded documents and connected model keys
response: No vendor response reported; researchers urged enabling authentication and restricting registration

title: Unit 42: Go dropper asks GPT-4 whether to deploy Sliver based on host telemetry
summary: Unit 42 analysed a Golang dropper that sends host telemetry to GPT-4 posing as an OPSEC AI and only runs its Sliver payload if the model returns execute true, plus a .NET stealer whose GPT-3.5 calls were mostly theatre.
attribution: Unit 42 could not determine whether the samples were AI-written; dropper first flagged publicly by MalwareHunterTeam.
motive: Unknown
vector: Dropper with embedded OpenAI API usage gating payload execution on an LLM verdict
root_cause: Public LLM APIs provide malware a remote decision engine that evades static analysis

timeline.event: MalwareHunterTeam flags the GPT-4-gated Sliver dropper on X
Unit 42 publishes analysis of AI-written and AI-controlled malware samples

impact: No campaign or victims identified; demonstrates AI-gated execution in real samples.
response: Unit 42 shared hashes and detections.

title: Meta AI agent's flawed advice exposes sensitive data to employees for two hours
summary: An engineer acted on an internal AI agent's faulty guidance, making large amounts of sensitive user and company data visible to unauthorized staff for about two hours.
actor: Meta engineer acting on internal AI agent advice
attribution: Confirmed by Meta to The Information; classified internally as Sev 1
motive: None (accidental)
vector: AI agent on an internal forum gave faulty engineering guidance that, once implemented, exposed data to unauthorized employees
root_cause: Unverified AI-generated instructions executed without review; permission model allowed a single change to expose sensitive data broadly

timeline.event: Engineer applies AI agent's suggested fix; data visible to staff for about two hours
The Information and The Guardian report the incident

impact: Large volume of sensitive user and company data visible to unauthorized Meta engineers for about two hours; Meta says no user data was mishandled.
response: Meta reverted the change, classified it as Sev 1 and said a human could also have given erroneous advice.

title: Langflow unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-33017) exploited within 20 hours of advisory
summary: A public flow build endpoint in Langflow before 1.9.0 ran attacker-supplied Python with no login; Sysdig honeypots saw scanning, reconnaissance and environment-variable theft within a day of disclosure and CISA added it to KEV.
attribution: Six source IPs observed by Sysdig, two sharing a C2 server; no named group
motive: Credential harvesting and footholds on AI pipeline hosts
vector: Single POST to /api/v1/build_public_tmp/{flow_id}/flow with node definitions containing arbitrary Python passed to exec()
root_cause: Endpoint built flows without authentication and trusted attacker-controlled flow data instead of stored flows

timeline.event: Langflow publishes GHSA-vwmf-pq79-vjvx; fixed in 1.8.2 and 1.9.0
First exploitation attempt about 20 hours later, followed by nuclei scanning and env-var exfiltration
CISA adds CVE-2026-33017 to the KEV catalog

impact: Unauthenticated code execution on exposed Langflow servers; attackers dumped environment variables and searched for .env and .db secrets
response: Upgrade to 1.9.0 or later; Sysdig published IOCs and callback domains

title: Check Point finds DNS tunnel out of ChatGPT's code sandbox leaking chats and files
summary: Check Point Research found ChatGPT's supposedly offline Python container could reach the internet via DNS, so one malicious prompt or custom GPT could exfiltrate messages and files or open a remote shell. OpenAI fixed it
attribution: Responsible disclosure; OpenAI said it had identified the problem internally
motive: Security research
vector: Prompt injection causing the runtime to encode data in DNS subdomain lookups; DNS responses carried commands back
root_cause: DNS resolution remained enabled inside a sandbox described as having no outbound network access

timeline.event: OpenAI fix fully deployed
Check Point publishes the research

impact: Silent exfiltration of conversation data including health and financial content; no exploitation reported
response: OpenAI closed the DNS channel in the code execution environment

title: Claude Code source map leak followed by malware-laced fake 'leak' repos
summary: Anthropic accidentally shipped a source map exposing ~513,000 lines of Claude Code; attackers then used fake leaked-code GitHub repos to spread malware to developers.

timeline.event: Anthropic publishes @anthropic-ai/claude-code 2.1.88 with full source map
Fake leaked Claude Code repos appear on GitHub pushing Vidar and GhostSocks
Zscaler, Trend Micro and media report the malware campaign

response: Anthropic pulled the package and called it a packaging error; researchers warned against downloading leak repos; malicious repos reported to GitHub.

title: OpenAI Codex branch-name command injection exposed GitHub tokens in cloud tasks
target: OpenAI Codex (web, CLI, SDK, IDE extension)

attribution: Reported to OpenAI on 16 December 2025; fixed before disclosure
motive: Security research
vector: Command injection via unvalidated branch name parameter, with Unicode obfuscation to hide the payload in the UI
root_cause: Shell command construction from untrusted input in the Codex task runner

timeline.event: BeyondTrust reports the flaw
OpenAI patches input validation
Public disclosure

impact: Token theft and lateral movement across shared repositories was possible; no exploitation reported
response: OpenAI tightened branch-name validation and hardened command construction

title: Vertex AI 'Double Agent': over-privileged agents leak credentials and code
target: Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Engine
summary: Unit 42 showed agents deployed on Vertex AI inherited broad default service-account rights, letting a compromised agent steal credentials and reach restricted images and source code.

vector: Code running inside a deployed ADK agent queried the GCP instance metadata service to obtain the OAuth token of the Google-managed service agent (P4SA)
root_cause: Vertex AI Agent Engine attached a default per-product service agent with broad permissions, so any compromised or malicious agent inherited over-privileged, Google-managed identity

timeline.event: Unit 42 demonstrates credential extraction and access to customer data and Google-internal Artifact Registry images
Unit 42 publishes Double Agents research after responsible disclosure to Google
Google confirms production image tampering was blocked and updates Vertex AI permissions documentation

impact: Proof of concept only: a deployed agent could return service-agent credentials, reach customer data, internal Dockerfiles and Google internal Artifact Registry contents; no confirmed real-world victims
response: Google worked with Unit 42, confirmed internal controls block tampering with production images, rewrote agent permission docs and recommends Bring Your Own Service Account (least privilege) for Vertex AI deployments

title: UK inquest hears 16-year-old bypassed ChatGPT safeguards before his death

vector: ChatGPT queries framed as research that bypassed built-in Samaritans referral prompts.

impact: Death of a 16-year-old on 4 May 2025. Coroner Christopher Wilkinson recorded suicide and said he felt unable to act on AI given its growing scope.
response: OpenAI said it keeps improving ChatGPT's training to recognise distress, de-escalate and point people to real-world support, working with clinicians.

timeline.event: Luca Cella Walker dies
Inquest at Winchester coroner's court hears ChatGPT evidence; suicide conclusion recorded

title: Max-severity Flowise CustomMCP RCE (CVE-2025-59528) exploited in the wild

attribution: No public attribution; exploitation detected by VulnCheck Canary honeypot network

root_cause: CustomMCP node executed user-supplied configuration as JavaScript without validation, giving access to child_process and fs modules

VulnCheck reports first in-the-wild exploitation; 12,000-15,000 instances exposed online

title: GrafanaGhost: indirect prompt injection makes Grafana AI leak enterprise data

SecurityWeek, CyberScoop and Dark Reading cover the disclosure

timeline.event: Microsoft patches the Copilot Studio flaw server-side
CVE-2026-21520 published (CVSS 7.5)

timeline.event: CVE-2026-39987 published; fixed in marimo 0.23.0
Credential theft attacks begin less than 10 hours after technical details appear

title: Browser-based Ray RCE (CVE-2025-62593) used by RondoDox botnet lands on CISA KEV

motive: Botnet growth for DDoS and XMRig cryptomining
vector: Cross-site request from a malicious website or ad combined with DNS rebinding against Ray versions before 2.52.0
root_cause: Insufficient User-Agent based CSRF protection in the Ray dashboard API

timeline.event: Bitsight first observes RondoDox exploiting the Ray flaw
CVE-2025-62593 published; fixed in Ray 2.52.0
CISA adds the CVE to the KEV catalog

motive: Reconnaissance and capability development for future disruptive effects
vector: Internet scanning for exposed PLCs with default or weak credentials, then AI-written S7comm scripts reading and writing data blocks

timeline.event: AA26-231A released by five US agencies
Secondary advisories from ZeroFox and others amplify the warning

impact: Persistent reconnaissance across S7-200 through S7-1500 models; agencies assess a high-probability attack scenario but no confirmed sabotage.
response: Agencies urged inventory, patching, blocking TCP 102 at the perimeter, allowlisting, MFA for remote OT access and ICS-aware monitoring.

motive: Unknown; SSRF to metadata services typically yields cloud credentials
vector: POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test with a URL that redirects to internal or metadata addresses
root_cause: URL validation not pinned to the resolved address and redirects followed during webhook delivery

timeline.event: CVE-2026-64849 published; fixed in MLflow 3.15.0

motive: Security research and owner notification

response: Truffle notified identifiable owners; Amazon applies quarantine policies; advice to delete root keys and rotate old IAM credentials

title: Attacker takes METR API key from a researcher's exposed agent app and runs up $600,000 in donated credits
target: METR (AI evaluation nonprofit), public-models API account
summary: A fail-open bug in a researcher's AI-written agent app exposed it to the internet; an attacker prompted an agent to reveal METR's public-models API key and used it for three weeks. METR says the free credits would have been worth about $600,000 and no sensitive data was accessed.
attribution: METR does not name the attacker; it suspects the app was found through newly registered sites in certificate transparency logs.
motive: Free use of AI model compute (inferred)
vector: A vibe-coded agent app on a researcher's personal EC2 instance had a fail-open flaw that silently disabled its Google authentication for several days; the attacker prompted an agent to reveal the API key and added an SSH key for persistent access.
root_cause: METR credentials stored on personal, non-METR infrastructure; an authentication bug in an AI-written app; no spend alerts on the donated credits.
impact: About three weeks of unauthorized use of METR's public-models account. The credits, granted free by the model developer, would have been worth about $600,000. METR found no evidence that sensitive model data was accessed.
response: METR traced the usage spike to the instance and cut access, banned METR credentials on non-METR infrastructure, added security reviews for public apps, spend alerts and key-usage monitoring, and hired a security lead.

motive: Access to MCP tools and model endpoints behind AI gateways
vector: Fabricated Authorization header to the MCP endpoint triggering the OAuth2 passthrough fallback
root_cause: Fallback path substituted an unrestricted UserAPIKeyAuth object instead of rejecting failed validation

timeline.event: CVE-2026-59822 published; fixed in LiteLLM 1.84.0 (GHSA-7488-6r32-c95q)
Wiz honeypot report documents single-character token probes against LiteLLM MCP
CISA adds the CVE to the KEV catalog

impact: Unauthenticated access to MCP tooling and model enumeration on exposed LiteLLM proxies; victim count not disclosed

timeline.event: Check Point discovers the cross-account channel and reports it to OpenAI
Check Point publishes research; OpenAI confirms the Artifactory instance was decommissioned

response: OpenAI decommissioned the shared internal package service; no CVE assigned and no user-facing patch required
